_note: Starting catalogue only. Ratings are the author's judgement (1-5), not measured. ALWAYS verify live with gh (recent outside merges, CONTRIBUTING, AI policy, DCO/CLA) before recommending. Add or remove orgs freely. `legal` is a best guess (cla/dco/none/varies): confirm in CONTRIBUTING before the student commits.

orgs.name: Zulip
orgs.notes: Famous for mentoring and a detailed contributor guide.

orgs.name: Oppia
orgs.notes: Structured onboarding for newcomers; GSoC participant.

orgs.name: scikit-learn
orgs.notes: Easy issues are claimed fast; docs and tests are good entry points.

orgs.name: NumPy / SciPy (NumFOCUS)
orgs.notes: Docs and small bug fixes welcomed; reviews can be slow.

orgs.name: Django
orgs.notes: Work goes through Trac tickets; read the contributing guide closely.

orgs.name: Kubernetes
orgs.notes: CNCF; contributor licence agreement required; large SIG-based community. Start with docs or kubernetes/website.

orgs.name: Prometheus
orgs.notes: CNCF; DCO; many small client libraries and exporters.

orgs.name: OpenTelemetry
orgs.notes: CNCF; one repo per language; CLA via EasyCLA.

orgs.name: OpenSSF
orgs.notes: Linux Foundation; Scorecard and related tools; security focus.

orgs.name: Rust language
orgs.notes: Has an explicit mentoring label system; compiler builds are heavy.

orgs.name: Home Assistant
orgs.notes: Huge integration surface; fixes for single integrations are small.

orgs.name: Mozilla
orgs.notes: Uses Bugzilla as well as GitHub; good-first-bug workflow.

orgs.name: Apache Software Foundation
orgs.notes: Each project differs; mailing-list culture; GSoC participant.
